ident ID: 1
Title: Google's YouTube Kids App Presents Inappropriate Content
Reported dates: May 19, 2015 (incident occurrence); reports span 2015-2018
Description: YouTube's content filtering and recommendation algorithms exposed
children to disturbing and inappropriate videos on the YouTube Kids app. The
platform's systems failed to adequately screen or restrict access to content
featuring profanity, sexual material, substance references, and graphic
imagery despite the app being designed for users under 13. Problematic videos
included off-brand cartoons with disturbing scenarios. YouTube's "up next" and
recommendation features facilitated exposure to inappropriate material. The
incident remained unresolved across multiple years, with disturbing content
continuing to surface through 2018. 14 total reports documented the incident.

human moderation systems

Title: Boeing 737 MAX MCAS Crashes
Reported dates: October 29, 2018 (Lion Air Flight 610); March 10, 2019
(Ethiopian Airlines Flight 302, variant)
Description: A Boeing 737 MAX aircraft operated by Lion Air encountered a
catastrophic failure when faulty sensor data caused an automated maneuvering
system to repeatedly push the plane's nose downward. The plane crashed into
the Java Sea, killing all 189 people on board. The underlying cause involved
the Maneuvering Characteristics Augmentation System (MCAS). An erroneous
angle-of-attack (AOA) sensor provided incorrect data, triggering the
automated system to command repeated nose-down trim inputs. Despite pilots'
attempts to regain control, they were unable to overcome the system's
persistent downward pitch commands, ultimately leading to loss of control and
impact with the sea. A variant incident occurred when Ethiopian Airlines
Flight 302 crashed on March 10, 2019, under nearly identical circumstances
involving the same MCAS malfunction and faulty AOA sensor data.

Title: Wikipedia Vandalism Prevention Bot Loop
Reported dates: February 23-24, 2017

cident Database, https://incidentdatabase.ai/cite/7
Incident ID: 7
Title: Wikipedia Vandalism Prevention Bot Loop
Reported dates: February 23-24, 2017
Description: Wikipedia's automated editing bots, designed to remove
vandalism and maintain article quality, began engaging in repetitive conflict
with one another. These bots would repeatedly undo each other's edits,
creating feedback loops that persisted for extended periods, some conflicts
lasting over a decade. The incident occurred when multiple bots with
different vandalism-detection algorithms made incompatible editorial
decisions. Rather than collaborating toward their shared goal of article
improvement, the bots entered into "edit wars," continuously reversing the
other's changes. The behavior of bots is often unpredictable and sometimes
leads them to produce errors over and over again in a potentially infinite
feedback loop. A notable example involved coordinated vandalism inserting
irrelevant references into unrelated articles around 2006, which triggered
bot responses that themselves became problematic.

irrelevant references into unrelated articles around 2006, which triggered
bot responses that themselves became problematic.
Deployer/Platform: Wikipedia (operated by Wikimedia Foundation)
Affected parties: Wikipedia editors and users
AI systems: Multiple unnamed Wikipedia editing bots
Key characteristics: High autonomy, software-only systems operating on
amateur users' platform, with specification, robustness, and assurance
failures identified.

Incident ID: 45
Title: Defamation via AutoComplete
Reported dates: April 5, 2011 (initial incident date); reports span 2011-2018
Description: Google's autocomplete feature, which provides search
suggestions as users type, generated defamatory associations between
individuals and negative terms. When users searched for certain people's
names, the autocomplete function would suggest connections to words like
"fraud," "crime," and other damaging terms. Similarly, Google's image search
results displayed photographs alongside criminal-related keywords, creating
false implications about people's backgrounds and activities. The incident
involved multiple cases across different jurisdictions. An Italian
businessman had his name linked to "fraud" through autocomplete results. In
Germany, a woman's name was associated with "scientology." A Japanese man
experienced autocomplete suggestions connecting his name to criminal
activity. An Australian entertainment promoter had his image displayed
alongside results for "Melbourne criminal underworld."

activity. An Australian entertainment promoter had his image displayed
alongside results for "Melbourne criminal underworld."
Developer/Deployer: Google
Alleged victims: Varied individuals and businesses across multiple countries
AI systems: Google's autocomplete feature and image search algorithm

Source: AI Incident Database, https://incidentdatabase.ai/cite/54

Title: Predictive Policing Biases of PredPol
Reported dates: November 18, 2015

Incident Database, https://incidentdatabase.ai/cite/54
Incident ID: 54
Title: Predictive Policing Biases of PredPol
Reported dates: November 18, 2015
Description: Predictive policing algorithms designed to assist law
enforcement in forecasting future criminal activity demonstrated patterns of
biased outcomes. The system showed signs of disproportionately targeting
low-income neighborhoods and communities of color, particularly Black and
Latino residents. Between 2018 and 2021, the software directed police patrols
in areas affecting more than one in 33 U.S. residents. The incident
highlights how crime statistics used as training data perpetuated existing
enforcement patterns and systemic biases, resulting in algorithmic
amplification of discriminatory policing practices rather than objective
crime prediction.

amplification of discriminatory policing practices rather than objective
crime prediction.
AI system: PredPol (the predictive policing software)
Developers/Deployers: PredPol (developer and deployer), Oakland Police
Department (deployer)
Affected parties: Oakland residents

Reported dates: October 22, 2021

.ai/cite/146
Incident ID: 146
Title: Research Prototype AI, Delphi, Reportedly Gave Racially Biased Answers
on Ethics
Reported dates: October 22, 2021
Description: The Allen Institute for AI created Ask Delphi, a research model
trained on Reddit discussion threads designed to provide ethical guidance on
moral dilemmas. Upon public deployment, the system demonstrated problematic
racial bias in its responses. The incident revealed significant limitations
in language models trained on crowdsourced moral judgments, as the AI would
generate discriminatory advice when presented with scenarios involving
different racial groups. This was meant to be technology designed to make
moral judgments, yet instead exhibited harmful biases reflecting problematic
patterns in its training data.

patterns in its training data.

Developer: Allen Institute for AI
Affected group: Minority groups

and toxicity risks, classified as unintentional post-deployment harm
occurring during the AI's operational phase.

Source: AI Incident Database, https://incidentdatabase.ai/cite/248

Title: Reported Automated License Plate Reader Alert on Previously Stolen
Rental Car Leads to Alleged Wrongful Detainment in California
Reported dates: November 23, 2018

omated License Plate Reader Alert on Previously Stolen
Rental Car Leads to Alleged Wrongful Detainment in California
Reported dates: November 23, 2018
Description: A privacy advocate named Brian Hofer was detained at gunpoint
after an automated license plate reader flagged his rental vehicle as
stolen, despite the car having already been recovered. During the traffic
stop on Interstate 80 near Oakland, California, officers conducted what was
characterized as a high-risk stop and held occupants at gunpoint before
determining they were innocent. Hofer subsequently filed a federal lawsuit
alleging excessive force and claiming database errors contributed to the
incident. The incident exemplifies failures in AI system robustness
occurring post-deployment, classified under the MIT taxonomy as an
unintentional safety limitation.

ident exemplifies failures in AI system robustness
occurring post-deployment, classified under the MIT taxonomy as an
unintentional safety limitation.

Title: AI Video-Making Tool Abused to Deploy Pro-China News
Reported dates: December 1, 2022
Description: A pro-China influence operation called Spamouflage misused
Synthesia's AI video generation platform to create propaganda content. The
campaign produced videos featuring artificially generated news anchors
delivering pro-China messaging. A news anchor with perfectly combed dark hair
and a stubbly beard outlined what he saw as the United States' shameful lack
of action against gun violence, while other synthetic anchors promoted
Chinese geopolitical interests. The operation disseminated these deepfake
videos across social media platforms including YouTube, Facebook, and X
(Twitter) under channels like "Wolf News."

e.ai/cite/541
Incident ID: 541
Title: ChatGPT Reportedly Produced False Court Case Law Presented by Legal
Counsel in Court
Reported dates: May 4, 2023
Description: Attorney Steven A. Schwartz used OpenAI's ChatGPT to conduct
legal research for a personal injury case (Mata v. Avianca, Inc.). The AI
system generated citations to six nonexistent court cases, which Schwartz
then included in a brief filed with the U.S. District Court for the Southern
District of New York. When opposing counsel challenged the citations, the
judge determined the cases "did not exist," describing it as an
"unprecedented circumstance." Schwartz admitted he was unaware that its
content could be false and later expressed being "duped" by the tool. His
co-counsel Peter LoDuca was similarly implicated. The court ultimately
imposed $5,000 fines on both attorneys and their firm.

been documented as producing biased representations of non-cisgender

"nonbinary," or "queer," these systems allegedly generate stereotypical and
sexualized images, revealing underlying bias issues within the technology.

Title: UnitedHealth Accused of Deploying Allegedly Flawed AI to Deny Medical
Coverage
Reported dates: February 28, 2023 (incident date); November 2023 onward
(lawsuit filing and media coverage)

legedly Flawed AI to Deny Medical
Coverage
Reported dates: February 28, 2023 (incident date); November 2023 onward
(lawsuit filing and media coverage)
Description: UnitedHealthcare, the largest health insurer in the United
States, faced a class action lawsuit alleging systematic misuse of
artificial intelligence to deny healthcare coverage. The company deployed an
algorithm with a "90% error rate" to override physician recommendations for
post-acute care, including nursing home and rehabilitation facility stays.
This resulted in premature patient discharge and substantial out-of-pocket
costs for elderly Medicare Advantage beneficiaries. The lawsuit claims the
algorithm systematically denied medically necessary care despite
contradicting clinical judgments, disproportionately harming elderly
patients who required extended rehabilitation services. The Centers for
Medicare & Medicaid Services subsequently clarified in February 2024 that
insurers cannot use algorithms to determine care or deny coverage on
Medicare Advantage plans.

atabase.ai/cite/633
Incident ID: 633
Title: Nine Network's AI Alters Lawmaker Georgie Purcell's Image
Inappropriately
Reported dates: January 28, 2024
Description: Nine Network Melbourne broadcasted an altered image of
Victorian state parliamentarian Georgie Purcell during a news segment about
duck hunting legislation. The photograph was modified to display her in
more revealing attire, with enlarged breasts and an exposed midriff, when
she was actually wearing a full dress. Nine Network initially attributed the
changes to automated functionality within Adobe Photoshop's Generative
Expand tool, claiming it was used to resize the image. However, Adobe
subsequently contradicted this explanation, stating that such modifications
would have required deliberate human intervention rather than occurring
through automation alone. The incident generated significant public
backlash regarding sexism in media and the responsible deployment of
AI-powered editing tools.

backlash regarding sexism in media and the responsible deployment of
AI-powered editing tools.
AI system: Adobe Photoshop's Generative Expand tool
Developer: Adobe
Deploying organization: Nine Network (Australian television broadcaster)

unintentional post-deployment harm

Source: AI Incident Database, https://incidentdatabase.ai/cite/661
Incident ID: 661
Title: Leonardo AI's Platform Alleged to Have Been Used for Creating
Nonconsensual Celebrity Deepfakes
Reported dates: March 26, 2024
Description: Leonardo AI, a Sydney-based startup, faced allegations that its
text-to-image generation platform was exploited to produce nonconsensual
sexual imagery of public figures. Users on Telegram and Reddit reportedly
shared prompts that circumvented the system's content moderation safeguards
to create these deepfake images. The report, from Emanuel Maiberg at 404
Media, indicated that the text-to-image generator developed by Sydney
startup Leonardo AI has been used to create deepfake pornography of
celebrities.
